choices.label: Follow Mara — go down to the basement

events.summary: 11:47 PM. A knock at the door.
You open the door. Mara steps in, dripping, and closes it behind her.
Mara spoke a cryptic remark about the key.
Mara took the bus ticket from the player's pocket.
Mara wrote four digits on the bus ticket.
You dial 1148. The padlock on 07 opens.
You climb past the last landing and shoulder the roof door open. Someone is on the stairs below you.
Mara ascended to the roof and approached the player.
The storm raged as the other you surveyed the roof.
The brass key unexpectedly transferred to the other you.
The other you admitted their actions.

B.narration:
You take out the bus ticket.

“1148”

That wasn't there when you put it in your pocket. The handwriting isn't yours.

The dark air presses against your surface.

You locked the door. Somewhere, you didn't.

prompt.content: You add one sentence of atmosphere to a quiet, literary horror story, in second person, present tense. Concrete senses only: sound, cold, light, smell, touch. No dialogue. Keep each sense literal: light shows only what can be seen; smells and sounds are sensed directly, never 'revealed' by light. Stay on the surfaces of where you are. No people, figures, faces or body parts, and nothing that suggests someone else is present.

Where you are: your apartment. With you: no one. The power is out; the only light is the storm's. Something impossible has just happened, and you have gone very still.
Write ONE short sentence (under 20 words) about what you sense around you. No names, no numbers, no quotes, no words in ALL CAPS, and don't explain anything. Nothing about your body, skin, hands or feet, and nothing about shoes. Never use these words: ozone, wet stone, damp stone, bare feet, skin, chill, viscous, face, hair, neck, cheek, lip, mouth, chest, spine, shoulder, arm, hand, finger, palm, wrist, foot, feet, toe, ankle, shoe, sock, teeth, tooth, eye, figure, someone, somebody, silhouette, shape, breath, breathing.

D.narration:
Mara turns the key over in the dark. The paper tag catches the storm light.

“TRUST HER”

That wasn't on the tag a minute ago. It's your handwriting. You don't remember writing it.

A low, resonant thrum vibrates through the concrete floor.

You followed Mara. Somewhere, you trusted Teo.

ending.text:
You open the door.

They don't come in at once. They look past you, at the night you kept, the way you'd look at a room you used to live in.

You look down at what the night left you. "1148" on the bus ticket, in Mara's handwriting. "TRUST HER" on the key's paper tag, in your own handwriting. Both made in a night you never lived.

Mara watches the two of you in the doorway. She has her witness now. For the first time tonight, she sits down.

In 6D, Teo's chain slides back. He opens his door to the empty hall and listens, and whatever he hears, he isn't afraid of it. "Finally," he says.

They step inside. You step back. There are two of you in the doorway, and the door won't close until one of you leaves.
changed: The brass key is in Mara's hand, beside you. And it is in your hand. You can feel both, like holding one thing in two hands.
Your bus ticket is in your hand. It always was.
Mara is beside you. She looks relieved, and very tired, like someone who has been holding a door shut for a long time.
